article.story: BOWLING GREEN, Ky. -- — Nick Minicucci threw for 414 yards and four touchdowns, with 183 yards and two scores going to Sean Wilson, and Delaware beat Western Kentucky 35-21 on Tuesday night to snap a seven-game road losing streak. Minicucci, who matched Delaware’s single-game record with five passing touchdowns last week, set another program record against WKU for consecutive completions to start a game at 17 before finishing 32 of 38. Minicucci moved into fourth in program history with 6,459 career yards. Wilson made nine catches for an average of 20.3 yards for Delaware (4-4, 2-2 Conference USA), which entered No. 1 in passing offence in the conference with 258.0 yards per game. Wilson's touchdown catches went for 21 and 40 yards. Kaderris Roberts and Jo Silver also had a touchdown grab. Brock Glenn was 25 of 37 for 224 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions for Western Kentucky (3-5, 2-2). He also carried it 17 times for 129 yards. Ajay Allen had 73 yards rushing and a score. The first incomplete pass for either team — in 14 attempts — was an interception by Delaware CB Kevin Moore late in the first quarter. AJ Graham also secured his first career interception on the first play of the fourth quarter deep in Delaware territory. Up next Delaware: Plays at Kennesaw State on Nov. 7. article.story: ROME -- — Brady Koehler scored key baskets down the stretch and Notre Dame made a late comeback after trailing for most of the second half to beat Villanova 74-72 in the college basketball season opener in Rome on Sunday. Villanova standout Tyler Perkins fouled out with 16.3 seconds to go. He led the Wildcats with 18 points. The event — dubbed the Eternal City Tip-Off — included an audience with Villanova alumnus Pope Leo XIV for both teams and their fans on Saturday. Both teams are unranked in the preseason AP Top 25. Koehler and Braeden Smith led Notre Dame, which has 10 new players, with 16 points each. Koehler’s dunk cut Villanova’s lead to one point with 1:36 remaining and Logan Duncomb hit a 3-pointer with 1:08 to go to give Notre Dame its first lead of the second half, 70-68. Koehler sank two free throws to put the Fighting Irish up 74-70 with 4 seconds remaining and essentially seal it. Villanova is looking for a revival after four years without winning a game at the NCAA Tournament: A three-year absence followed the sudden retirement of Hall of Fame coach Jay Wright and then the Wildcats had a first-round loss to Utah State last season. Luigi Suigo, the 7-foot-3 Italian making his Villanova debut on home soil, had two dunks and showed his range with a 3-pointer to finish with seven points. When he scored, the arena announcer yelled, “Su-su-su Suigo.” The nonconference game between the two Catholic universities was played at the 11,000-seat Palazzo dello Sport, which is located about a half-hour drive from the Vatican. Villanova had many more fans in attendance. It’s a doubleheader and a women’s game between the two schools was up next. Up next Notre Dame faces another Catholic school in its home opener against Mercyhurst on Thursday. Villanova faces two more Catholic schools in its next two games: The Wildcats play Holy Cross in their home opener on Friday and then meet La Salle four days later. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
